Dimitris Papanikolaou We analyze firms' decisions to invest in incremental
focusing specifically on pharmaceutical research. We develop a new measure of drug novelty that is based on the chemical similarity between new drug candidates
existing drugs. We show that drug candidates that we identify as ex-ante novel are riskier investments
in the sense that they are subsequently less likely to be approved by the FDA. However
more valuable―they are more clinically effective; have higher patent citations; lead to more revenue
to higher stock market value. Using variation in the expansion of Medicare prescription drug coverage
we show that firms respond to a plausibly exogenous cash flow shock by developing more molecularly novel drug compounds
as opposed to more so-called "me-too" drugs. This pattern suggests that
firms perceive novel drugs to be more valuable ex-ante investments
but that financial frictions may hinder their willingness to invest in these riskier candidates. Keywords: Research
